before.title: AC Compressor Premature Failure
before.description: The AC compressor in the Outlander Sport frequently fails between 50,000 and 80,000 miles. The compressor clutch bearing seizes or the internal reed valves break, contaminating the AC system with metal debris.
before.solution: Replace the AC compressor, receiver/drier, and expansion valve. Flush the entire system to remove metal particles. Install an inline filter on the liquid line to protect the new compressor from residual debris.

proposal.title: AC Compressor Premature Failure
proposal.description: The reviewed 309-row exact Outlander Sport manufacturer-communication corpus contains one broad multi-vehicle summary that mentions A/C compressor issues but supplies no condition, population, mechanism or repair. It does not establish recurring 2011-2020 compressor failure, a 50,000-80,000-mile range, clutch-bearing seizure, broken reed valves or metal contamination. Recall 15V233000 is a bounded 2011 blower-motor defect affecting defroster performance, not compressor evidence.
proposal.solution: Identify the refrigerant, compressor type and exact loss-of-cooling or noise complaint. Recover and weigh the charge, record high- and low-side pressures and temperatures, verify electrical command and supply, locate leakage and inspect recovered oil and refrigerant before assigning internal damage or contamination. Do not buy a compressor, receiver/drier, expansion valve, inline filter, refrigerant, oil or flush kit from this page; the failed component, contamination state and exact fitment must be proven first.
symptoms: charge, pressure, temperature and electrical results documented
leakage, clutch, control and internal paths separated

before.title: Battery drain / dead battery and no-start
before.description: Owners of 2015-era Outlander Sport models report repeated dead batteries, including the vehicle failing to start after sitting for a weekend and batteries needing replacement multiple times within low mileage. A parasitic electrical drain (rather than a simply weak battery) is frequently the culprit, alongside the usual battery/alternator/starter failures.
before.solution: Test for a parasitic draw (disconnect the negative cable when parked; if it restarts after reconnecting, hunt the drain). Replace a weak battery or failing alternator/starter as confirmed. Some dead-battery cases on 2015 models may be addressed under warranty - ask the dealer.
symptoms: clicking or no crank when starting

proposal.title: Battery drain / dead battery and no-start
proposal.description: The exact manufacturer corpus does not establish a 2015 Outlander Sport parasitic-drain defect, repeated weekend no-start pattern or repeated low-mileage battery replacement. Communications 10152871, 10159648 and 10159667 instead describe a cold-weather no-restart or failsafe condition with specified DTCs that may require anti-freezing ETV, CVT, injector or starter relays. Recall 17V609000 separately covers defective relays on certain 2015-2016 vehicles that can cause stall, reduced power or overheating. Neither source proves parasitic draw.
proposal.solution: Separate no-crank, crank-no-start and post-drive no-restart complaints. Load-test the battery, verify charging voltage and starter voltage drop, preserve DTCs, check recall and bulletin applicability, and measure key-off current only after all networks enter their specified sleep state before isolating a circuit. Do not disconnect the battery as a parasitic-draw test. Do not buy a battery, alternator, starter, relay or module from this page; the exact failed capacity, charging, cranking, relay or key-off-load path must be proven first.

before.title: CVT Judder and Hesitation
before.description: The Outlander Sport CVT develops a judder during low-speed acceleration and deceleration. The transmission hesitates when pulling away from stops, and the simulated shift points feel rough and inconsistent.
before.solution: Replace the CVT fluid with Mitsubishi DiaQueen CVTF-J4 every 30,000 miles. A TCM reprogram may smooth out the shift calibration. Avoid towing with the CVT-equipped models.

proposal.title: CVT Judder and Hesitation
proposal.description: Exact Mitsubishi communications support a bounded shudder or surge diagnostic path on certain 2015-2024 Outlander Sport vehicles with F1CJC/W1CJC CVT-8 transmissions. The evidence does not establish the frozen 2011-2026 population, universal deceleration judder, rough simulated shift points, a fixed 30,000-mile fluid interval or a blanket towing prohibition. Recall 16V563000 is a separate 2015-2016 software acceleration-delay condition.

On an applicable CVT-8, follow the current Mitsubishi test-drive, drive-data, hydraulic-pressure and belt-inspection sequence; separately verify specified fluid, level, cooler, leakage and recall completion. Use the VIN-specific maintenance and towing instructions. Do not buy CVT fluid, a valve body, belt-and-pulley assembly, cooler or transmission from this page; the exact population, service requirement and failed software, hydraulic or mechanical path must be proven first.

before.title: CVT shudder, slipping, and premature failure
before.description: The Jatco-built CVT used across most Outlander Sport years is prone to shuddering, jerking, hesitation when shifting from park to drive/reverse, whining or whirring noise during acceleration, and slipping (engine revs without proportional acceleration). Degraded CVT fluid and belt/chain wear are the primary drivers, and neglected fluid accelerates failure. Powertrain is consistently the most-complained-about area in NHTSA data for this model.
before.solution: Replace CVT fluid on a shortened interval (roughly every 30,000-60,000 miles rather than 'lifetime'). Persistent shudder may require a valve body or full CVT replacement. Earlier model years had a separate recall (16V-563) for a CVT control module causing delayed gear engagement.
symptoms: hesitation shifting into drive or reverse
RPM rises but car does not accelerate (slipping)

before.title: CVT software defect causes engine over-rev and stall at highway speed
before.description: On 2019-2022 Outlander Sport models with a CVT and a keyed (mechanical) ignition, a programming error in the CVT-ECU can misread a brief (0.1 second or longer) loss of the ignition power supply signal and command an erroneous gear ratio. At speeds above 62 mph this causes the engine to over-rev, which can drive a piston into an exhaust valve, permanently damaging the engine and causing it to stall while driving. Mitsubishi reported 31 engines needed replacement before the recall.
before.solution: Free dealer reflash of the CVT-ECU software under NHTSA recall 22V-563 / Mitsubishi SR-22-004. Owners should check their VIN at nhtsa.gov for an open recall; engines already damaged by the fault are repaired/replaced under the campaign.
symptoms: engine revs unexpectedly high above 62 mph
loss of power at highway speed

proposal.title: Windshield wiper motor/linkage water intrusion and corrosion
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 16V792000 covers certain 2011-2015 Outlander Sport vehicles whose wiper-motor breathing hole can admit water from the hood-to-windshield area and cause internal motor corrosion and failure. Recall 18V103000 separately covers certain 2011-2016 vehicles whose front wiper-link ball joint can corrode, separate and make the wipers inoperative. Both conditions reduce visibility, but their populations and remedies must remain distinct.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN against 16V792000 / SR-16-010 and 18V103000 / SR-18-004. An authorized Mitsubishi dealer performs the applicable free remedy: wiper-motor replacement under 16V792000, or wiper-link rod and motor-crank-arm replacement under 18V103000. Do not buy a wiper motor, linkage, crank arm or cowl part from this page; recall eligibility and the dealer inspection control the remedy.
symptoms: 2011-2016 VIN and both wiper recall histories verified
motor operation and link separation checked independently
recall completion and post-remedy function documented
affectedSystems: wiper-link ball joint, rod and crank arm
forward visibility in rain or snow
